picks.editorial_note: An AI model designed a bacteriophage used in the first-ever treatment of a patient with an antibiotic-resistant infection — a striking proof point that generative AI can move from drug discovery hype into an actual bedside intervention.
picks.title: This time, the virus is on the patient’s side. AI helped design it

picks.editorial_note: CSIRO's machine-learning imaging technique independently confirmed the iconic 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of the M87 black hole, with the validation published in Nature — a rare case of AI directly corroborating a landmark physics result.
picks.title: New CSIRO technique confirms iconic black hole image

picks.editorial_note: ARPA-H's $53M bet on an MIT-led team to use generative AI for discovering next-generation herbicide alternatives is a major federal investment aimed squarely at a chemical-safety and food-security problem.
picks.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers

picks.editorial_note: A $19M state grant builds Texas Tech a next-generation computing cluster integrating AI with high-fidelity simulation — a significant infrastructure investment tying AI research capacity directly to regional semiconductor strategy.
picks.title: Texas Tech Receives $19 Million Grant to Further Semiconductor Innovation | Texas Tech Now

picks.editorial_note: Atos and Inria's strategic partnership to push physical and agentic AI research into sovereign industrial applications signals a deliberate European push to convert academic AI research into domestic industrial and security capability.
picks.title: Atos and Inria enter into a strategic partnership to accelerate the transfer of research into sovereign industrial applications

picks.editorial_note: MIT CSAIL and CMU's 'Workspace Models' give robots a way to recall past observations without expensive recomputation, a meaningful step toward robots that can learn complex, multi-step skills efficiently.
picks.title: A new form of memory helps robots learn complex skills

picks.editorial_note: Michigan Tech and UCLA's finding that AI models need far less training data than assumed to predict materials' electronic structures could meaningfully lower the cost and barrier of AI-driven materials discovery.
picks.title: Less Data, Faster Discovery: Researchers Rethink AI’s Role in Developing New Materials

picks.editorial_note: TU Wien's study of a 15-year-old machine learning recidivism risk tool used in Catalonia found that equally accurate scoring systems can produce very different real-world outcomes — a concrete warning for governments already relying on such algorithms in sentencing and parole decisions.
picks.title: Im Zweifel für das geringere Risiko

picks.editorial_note: UNSW and Surf Life Saving Australia's RipEye tool shows AI moving into public safety in a tangible way, pairing automated rip-current detection with public education to directly reduce drowning risk.
picks.title: Using AI to help learn about and spot dangerous rips

picks.editorial_note: MIT's new quantization method targeting the KV cache memory bottleneck in large language models, headed for NeurIPS, addresses one of the most practical obstacles to cheaper, faster LLM inference at scale.
picks.title: Faster data compression through quantization
